review.note: Retracted in M21 both as outside the atlas — this is French Guinea, Conakry and not Bissau — and for having only one edge. The second reason is gone under the rule of 4 September 2026, and the first was never quite right: the atlas already keeps the referendum of 1958 for the same Portuguese reason. The other four Conakry records the import caught stay retracted, having no edge at all.

title: 1957 Guinean Territorial Assembly election
summary: Elections to the Territorial Assembly of French Guinea on 31 March 1957, the first under the loi-cadre that gave the French African territories elected governments of their own, gave Sékou Touré's Democratic Party of Guinea 56 of the 60 seats on a turnout of about sixty per cent. It made him the head of a territorial government and the only interlocutor France had in Conakry. It is in the atlas for what he did with that position eighteen months later: Guinea was the one territory to vote No to de Gaulle's community in September 1958, took its independence at once, and became the rear base without which the PAIGC's war in Portuguese Guinea is hard to imagine.
